emails.subject: Query - Study INN-123 - Site 101 - Subject HV-004 Lab Result
emails.body:
Hi David,

Hope you are having a good week.

We have an automated query in the Medidata EDC for subject HV-004, a healthy volunteer in Part A. The query is for an out-of-range Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT) value of 52 U/L from the Week 4 visit. The upper limit of normal is 50 U/L.

The subject is asymptomatic and all other liver function tests are within the normal range. Can you please advise if this is considered clinically significant and provide guidance on how to resolve the query?

Query ID: 884321

Thanks for your help,

Brenda Walsh
Clinical Research Coordinator
Westwood Clinical Research Center

emails.subject: RE: Query - Study INN-123 - Site 101 - Subject HV-004 Lab Result
emails.body:
Hi Brenda,

Thank you for flagging this.

I have reviewed the data and consulted with our Medical Monitor, Dr. Jenkins (cc'd). Given that this is a minor elevation (1.04x ULN) in an asymptomatic healthy volunteer with all other LFTs being normal, this finding is considered Not Clinically Significant (NCS).

Please close the query in Medidata with the following comment: "Value confirmed as accurate. Per sponsor, this is not clinically significant."

Let me know if you have any further questions.

Best regards,

David Chen
Clinical Research Associate
Innovate Pharma

description: A site coordinator emails the CRA with a question about a specific lab result for a healthy volunteer in Part A that is flagged as out-of-range in the EDC system. The CRA investigates the query, consults with the study's medical monitor, and responds to the site confirming that the value is not clinically significant and provides instructions on how to close the query.
